Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'common' (potions.py:190), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy.

Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583-616), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:16,263-289). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False, so CombatState.use_potion passes target=None (combat.py:608) and the potion applies to ctx.player (potions.py:192-197)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.AnyPlayer in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

ExtraHoverTips.maps_to: no counterpart; the sim has no hover-tip surface
ExtraHoverTips.rationale: ExtraHoverTips / HoverTipFactory / PotionModel.HoverTip are the potion tooltip's keyword lines. Waived under the shared contract's presentation exclusion, not under any unreachability claim.

CanonicalVars (protected override, Speed.rationale: `new PowerVar<DexterityPower>(5m)` -- the var names DexterityPower while OnUse applies SpeedPotionPower (SpeedPotion.cs:22 vs :30), the same var/class split FlexPotion has. 5, no ascension branch.

OnUse (protected override, SpeedPotion.c.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<SpeedPotionPower>(ctx, target, Dexterity.BaseValue, Owner.Creature, null)` -> `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, player, SpeedPotionPower, 5, applier=player)`. The class is SpeedPotionPower (a TemporaryDexterityPower), not DexterityPower -- the difference between this potion and dexterity_potion -- and the port applies the right one. The power itself is audit/records/power/speed_potion.json's (binding rule 3).
